question: Do recoverable evidence projections and preauthorized deterministic tool sequences improve the quality-cost frontier of the same native LLM harness?
baseline: Contemporary pinned native harness with ordinary tools and normal context behavior; identical safety controls and evidence access
candidate: Factorial comparison: recoverable receipts (R), deterministic tool flow (D), and their combination (RD)
learner_locus: Agent system state and optional procedures, not hosted model weights
retention_boundary: Separate fresh-task sessions and repeated sequential-workload sessions; no memory or skill leakage across arms

dataset.source: Prospective generated software repair and evidence-retrieval task families; versions unresolved
dataset.holdout: Evaluator-controlled unseen families and recombinations; development feedback never reclassified as holdout

resource_caps.per_episode_time_and_token_limits: Must be fixed before any provider run

protocol.stopping_rule: Freeze finite task, repeat, retry, time and resource limits before execution; no success-based early stopping. Preserve failed, censored and unknown outcomes.
freeze_required: task generator and family split identities
model and harness versions and supported context-control surface
arm order and fresh versus sequential session schedules
independent repeats and session-level analysis unit
quality noninferiority margin and material cost effect
usage schema including cache write/read and reasoning accounting
evidence retention privacy access and recovery policies

notes: Design only. HELIX is external exploratory evidence, not our baseline or a reproduced result. EXP-0001 through EXP-0004 remain unchanged. No model runs, installations, automatic API fallback or release are authorized by this manifest.
